issue: Visual-grammar mismatch: the figure is drawn as a vertical stack of equal-width bars with a single point-year per row, which reads as a layered substrate / causal sequence. The caption must explicitly rescue the reader from that false inference ('not a causal lineage and not a substrate stack: a later stage does not require the one before it, and the eras overlap'). Compounding this, the caption's claims that dates are 'approximate era markers' and that 'the eras overlap' are not visually encoded at all: each row shows one point year, not a span, so no overlap is depicted. The layout therefore both invites a wrong reading and fails to show the property the caption emphasizes.
evidence: Rendered page 461: nine full-width bars stacked with no gaps (Transformer ~2017 ... Agent Fleet ~2026), each with a single year label on the right and no horizontal duration. Caption: 'the ascending order is a chronology of selected milestones, not a causal lineage and not a substrate stack: a later stage does not require the one before it, and the eras overlap.' The authors' own 'not a substrate stack' warning confirms the geometry induces that misreading.
acceptance_test: Redesign so the geometry cannot be read as a stack/lineage and so era spans (and overlaps) are visible: use a horizontal time axis with each milestone drawn as a bar spanning its approximate era (start-end), rows ordered by time rather than by layer. After the change, a reader must not be able to infer 'Agent System requires Agent requires Tool-Using Model' from the layout, and at least one visible overlap between eras must appear.

issue: Edge-label placement in the Pattern-Measurement-Feedback loop: the 'validate vs 800 ms target' arrow is drawn on the DERIVED->PATTERN edge (box 2 -> box 3). Read literally this puts SLO validation before the pattern is chosen and invites the category-error inference that the bandwidth-bound *diagnosis* (box 2) is being validated against a latency target. In this loop the measurement that checks the SLO logically follows pattern application (box 3) and belongs on the PATTERN->ASSUMPTION feedback edge; that edge is instead labeled 'adjust + pick pattern', which also misplaces 'pick pattern' (pattern selection is box 3's output, not the feedback action).
evidence: Rendered page 445: green arrow box2->box3 labeled 'validate vs 800 ms target'; red arrow box3->box1 labeled 'adjust + pick pattern' / 'feedback'. Caption: 'the validate step compares the load test's measured TTFT p99 against the hypothesis criterion (TTFT p99 < 300 ms, S8 Step 3) under the capstone's p99 <= 800 ms TTFT target (S8 Step 0).'
acceptance_test: Relabel/move edges so the SLO comparison is unambiguously tied to a measured p99 after the pattern, and pattern selection is unambiguously box 3's output: e.g., label the box2->box3 edge 'diagnosis drives selection' and put 'validate measured p99 vs 800 ms target' on the box3->box1 feedback edge (drop 'pick pattern' from that edge). A reader must not be able to read the diagram as 'the bandwidth-bound diagnosis is validated against 800 ms.'

issue: Evidence-label inconsistency: the figure is purely authored (y-axis 'Authored intensity (0-1)'), yet its caption carries no [ILLUSTRATIVE] tag, while other conceptual/illustrative figures in the same book do (Fig A.3 caption and in-figure note carry [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]; Fig A.1 caption carries [DERIVED]). A reader applying the book's three-axis taxonomy (Ch 4 / Appendix A) would expect an authored, non-measured figure to be tagged.
evidence: Rendered page 434: y-axis label 'Authored intensity (0-1)'; caption 'FIGURE 26.1: Workload fingerprints on the six axes. per-axis 0-1 scale; compare within an axis, not across axes.' - no [ILLUSTRATIVE]/[DERIVED] tag. Compare page 461 Fig A.3 caption '[ILLUSTRATIVE] conceptual chronology; [DERIVED] era markers' and page 451 Fig A.1 caption 'fractions are [DERIVED] from the 1P model-card counts'.
acceptance_test: Add an [ILLUSTRATIVE] tag (plus a clause that the values are authored to depict relative intensity, not measured) to Fig 26.1's caption, matching the tagging practice of Figs A.1 and A.3.

issue: Visual composition / excess whitespace: the x-axis runs 0-10 while the largest bar is 5.6%, leaving roughly the right 44% of the plot empty. Not a correctness error (a round 0-10 limit is defensible), but the empty region shrinks the bars and reduces the visibility of the small inter-family spread (3.7 vs 4.6 vs 4.8 vs 5.6) the figure is meant to convey.
evidence: Rendered page 451: x-axis ticks 0,2,4,6,8,10; bars end at ~3.7 (Kimi K3), ~4.6 (DeepSeek V4-Flash), ~4.8 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next), ~5.6 (GLM-5.3-Flash); the region from ~5.6 to 10 is blank.
acceptance_test: Tighten the x-axis to a round limit near the data max (e.g., 0-6 or 0-8) so the bars occupy most of the plot width and the 3.7-5.6% spread is more legible; confirm the per-row annotations (e.g., '2800B/104B active', the two-line Qwen note) still fit without wrapping or overlap.
